CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Project

bixverse.gpu is an R package providing GPU-accelerated algorithms (kNN search, k-means, PCA, Harmony, UMAP, tSNE, parametric UMAP, SCENIC, SEACells meta cells, Scrublet doublet detection, correlations) that plug into the bixverse / manifoldsR ecosystem. The heavy lifting is Rust, exposed to R via extendr. GPU code runs on WGPU via cubecl / burn, so it is portable across vendors (no CUDA required).

Common commands

Rextendr-based workflow. Run from an R session at the repo root:

devtools::load_all()          # build the Rust static lib + load the package
devtools::document()          # since rextendr 0.5.0 this also compiles Rust and regenerates R/extendr-wrappers.R from #[extendr] fns; use this after editing Rust
rextendr::clean()             # nuke cargo build artifacts (e.g. after Cargo.toml changes)
tinytest::test_package("bixverse.gpu")   # run the full test suite
tinytest::run_test_file("inst/tinytest/test_gpu_kmeans.R")  # run one test file

Rust builds live under src/rust/target/ and are always release (opt-level = 3), which is CRAN policy. DEBUG=1 is ignored by tools/config.R; do not add a debug path.

During development set DEV_BUILD=true. It keeps src/rust/target/ and the shared cargo registry warm between installs and drops LTO, which cuts a document() cycle from minutes to seconds. Still a release build, so do not benchmark or submit from one. It deliberately does not engage on a vendored build, where CARGO_HOME has to stay local for vendor-config.toml.

R CMD check runs in CI (.github/workflows/R-cmd-check.yml) on macOS and Ubuntu. Linux CI installs libvulkan1 / mesa-vulkan-drivers and sets WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan.

Formatting: R code uses air (air.toml present). Rust is stock cargo fmt.

Architecture

The package is a thin R shim over a Rust crate. Three layers, top-down:

  1. R user API (R/*.R): friendly, validated wrappers. sc_gpu.R (single-cell workflows, S7 generics dispatching on SingleCells / SingleCellsMultiModal from bixverse), scenic_gpu.R (SCENIC GRN inference, dispatching on SingleCells / MetaCells), seacells_gpu.R (SEACells meta cells, dispatching on SingleCells / SingleCellsSubset), scrublet_gpu.R (Scrublet doublet detection, dispatching on SingleCells), umap_gpu.R, tsne_gpu.R, parametric_umap.R, ml_gpu.R (k-means), nn_gpu.R (kNN graphs), utils.R (parse_verbosity). Argument checks use checkmate plus local checkmate_extensions.R, where each checkXParams() predicate is wrapped into an assertXParams() via checkmate::makeAssertionFunction (assertNnParamsGpu, assertUmapParamsGpu, assertTsneParamsGpu, and so on). Parameter builders live in param_wrappers.R (params_sc_cagra, params_sc_ivf, params_nn_gpu, params_umap_gpu, params_tsne_gpu, params_kmeans_gpu, params_parametric_umap, params_sc_harmony_v2_gpu): each returns a plain named list that the corresponding assert function then validates before it crosses into Rust. SCENIC and SEACells have no local builder: they reuse bixverse::params_scenic() / bixverse:::assertScenicParams() and bixverse::params_sc_seacells() / bixverse:::assertScSeacells() respectively.
  2. extendr bridge (R/extendr-wrappers.R): GENERATED by rextendr::document() from #[extendr] attributes in Rust; never edit by hand. Any change to a Rust-exposed function signature or doc comment requires re-running document().
  3. Rust crate (src/rust/, package name bixverse_gpu). src/lib.rs holds the top-level extendr_module! registration, the precision helpers (parse_precision, auto_precision, SAMPLE_THRESHOLD_HIGH_PRECISION) and the PUmapModel backend-agnostic wrapper. It also holds most #[extendr] entry points, but not all: pca_gpu.rs, harmony_gpu.rs, scenic_gpu.rs, scrublet_gpu.rs and seacells_gpu.rs each carry their own, registered through use <mod>; lines inside extendr_module! rather than fn lines. Subdirectories:
    • embeddings/: umap_gpu.rs, tsne_gpu.rs, parametric_umap.rs (neural-net UMAP with GPU and CPU backends), utils.rs (R list to Rust parameter structs).
    • single_cell/: knn_gpu.rs (CAGRA / IVF / exhaustive), pca_gpu.rs (sparse randomised SVD), harmony_gpu.rs, scenic_gpu.rs (in-memory, streaming and MetaCells GRN drivers), scrublet_gpu.rs, seacells_gpu.rs, sc_utils.rs (shared cell-mapping and kNN conversion helpers; only seacells_gpu.rs consumes them so far).
    • ml/clustering.rs: k-means.
    • utils.rs: R to Rust matrix converters (r_matrix_to_faer_fp32, faer_to_r_matrix, nearest_neighbours_to_rust).

Backends: - GpuBackend = Autodiff<Wgpu>: the WGPU/cubecl path for all “GPU” algorithms. - CpuBackend = Autodiff<Flex<f32>>: used by parametric UMAP on the CPU path. flex replaced the old ndarray backend for parametric UMAP.

Precision policy: UMAP/tSNE dispatch fp32 vs fp64 through parse_precision, which honours the user’s use_high_precision arg or falls back to auto_precision (fp64 above SAMPLE_THRESHOLD_HIGH_PRECISION = 100_000 samples). tSNE is called out as precision-sensitive.

For the sibling Rust crates that own the actual algorithms, see the next section.

External Rust crates

Three sibling crates (same maintainer) hold most of the real work. bixverse.gpu is largely a thin R interface into them. Knowing which crate owns what matters when hunting a bug or extending an algorithm; most GPU kernels do not live in this repo.

  • ann-search-rs: approximate nearest-neighbour crate. Owns CAGRA / IVF / exhaustive kNN plus shared SIMD and GPU-tensor infrastructure that the other sibling crates reuse. Many of the GPU primitives dispatched from here originate there, including the GPU k-means (ann_search_rs::gpu::k_means_gpu), which used to live in bixverse-rs. (feature: gpu)
  • bixverse-rs: Rust engine behind the whole bixverse ecosystem. This package consumes its GPU-accelerated pieces (linalg, PCA, Harmony, correlations, SCENIC, SEACells); the main non-GPU R-facing interface lives in the separate bixverse R package. (features: gpu, single-cell) It no longer owns the GPU k-means kernels, only the R-list parsing for them, via the KMeansGpuParamsFromR extension trait in bixverse_rs::gpu::gpu_r_wrappers.
  • manifolds-rs: manifold-learning crate. UMAP, tSNE, diffusion maps, PaCMAP, PHATE. Depends on ann-search-rs for kNN. GPU coverage is expanding: kNN searches are already GPU, and the UMAP optimiser now has a GPU path too. (features: parametric, gpu, plus fft_tsne off-Windows, see the h5 toolchain issue in the README)

During development src/rust/Cargo.toml wires two of these to local checkouts so you track their HEAD. bixverse-rs is a plain path dependency, nothing else in the graph depends on it. ann-search-rs cannot be: this crate, bixverse-rs and manifolds-rs all depend on it, and a path dep would resolve to a second copy whose types no longer match across the boundary. It goes through [patch.crates-io] instead, which unifies the whole graph. Note that bixverse-rs carries the same patch block, but patches only apply from the top-level manifest, so it has to be repeated here. Both the path dep and the patch block have to go before merging, otherwise CI cannot resolve them and the vendored offline build path breaks.

Conventions

  • kNN indices returned to R are 1-indexed. Rust returns 0-based and R adds 1 in nn_gpu.R::generate_knn_graph. Matrices returned to Rust are always cells x features / samples x features (row-major from R’s perspective).
  • Verbosity everywhere: 0L silent, 1L normal, 2L detailed. R-side accepts a boolean or 0/1/2; funnels through parse_verbosity() before crossing into Rust.
  • S3 classes: KMeansClusterGPU (in R/classes.R) implements manifoldsR::membership / get_centroids. ParametricUmapModel has print and predict methods and can be serialised via save_parametric_umap / load_parametric_umap (bytes are tagged 0=GPU, 1=CPU by rs_serialise_parametric_umap).
  • .onLoad in R/zzz.R calls S7::methods_register(). Do not remove it, the single-cell generics need it.
  • Package is lifecycle: experimental, which covers the whole R-facing surface. Do not put r lifecycle::badge("experimental") in hand-written roxygen; the badge only appears on the rs_* wrappers, where it comes from the Rust /// doc comments.

Writing style

Applies to every surface where prose lands in front of a reader: vignettes (.qmd), README, roxygen @description / @details, code comments, commit messages, PR titles and descriptions.

Hard rules:

  • No em-dashes, neither the ASCII nor the Unicode variant. Reads as AI-generated. Use commas, colons, semicolons, or full stops.
  • British English. normalise, randomised, centred, favour, analyse, colour.
  • No corporate filler: “leverages”, “utilises”, “seamlessly”, “cutting-edge”, “robust”, “state-of-the-art”, “empowers”, “enables”, “unlocks”, “delve into”.
  • No hedge stacks (“may sometimes potentially”), no filler transitions (“Furthermore”, “Moreover”, “It is worth noting that”), no throat-clearing intros (“In this section we will walk through”).
  • No trailing paragraphs that recap what the section just showed. The exception is a conclusion that adds something forward-looking (roadmap, caveats, what to try next).

Positive patterns:

  • Short sentences. Active voice. Contractions are fine and usually better.
  • Concrete over abstract, with numbers where possible. “25k points across 25 clusters in 32D” beats “a moderately sized clustered dataset”.
  • Admit weaknesses directly. “On Apple Silicon the GPU rarely blows the CPU out of the water” beats hedging around it.
  • Brief, specific editorialising is welcome (“gets painful fast”, “watch this space”). Once or twice per vignette, not per section.
  • Keep @param / @returns roxygen bullets terse and structured. The style rules above are for prose blocks.

Older files may still contain em-dashes from before this rule. Do not go on a retroactive rewriting spree, fix them when you touch the surrounding prose anyway.

Notes and non-obvious things

  • The document binary in src/rust/document.rs is invoked by Makevars after the lib build to regenerate wrappers during install. That’s why document.rs sits alongside Cargo.toml and has its own [[bin]] entry.
  • configure / configure.win plus tools/config.R and tools/msrv.R implement CRAN-friendly Rust detection and the vendored-crate offline build path (src/rust/vendor.tar.xz, generated at release time). Don’t hand-edit src/Makevars, it is generated from src/Makevars.in.
  • bixverse, bixverse.plots, manifoldsR are Remotes:. Assume they are installed from GitHub in dev environments.
